items: Item questions almost always need Item_ID plus the human-readable Item_Name/Item_Description in response_columns — never return Item_ID alone as the response. Plant_ID is a pipeline_column whenever the question mentions a plant/location or when more than one table is joined, but it is a response_column only if the user actually asked about plant. Status/material-status columns belong in pipeline_columns whenever the question filters or asks about active/inactive/valid items, even if not explicitly named.
bom: BOM questions are inherently parent/child: always include both the parent item and child/component item identifying columns in pipeline_columns, and prefer the child item's name/description (not just its ID) in response_columns. Quantity-per / usage-quantity columns are pipeline_columns whenever the question mentions how much, ratio, or usage; they only become response_columns if the question is specifically about quantities.
routing: Routing questions center on operation sequence — always keep the sequence/operation-number column in pipeline_columns so ORDER BY works correctly, and put it in response_columns whenever more than one operation row is returned. Routing/operation description columns should be preferred over raw operation codes in response_columns unless the user explicitly asked for codes.
erp_operation: This is a small lookup/master table — when in doubt, include every non-audit column in pipeline_columns; the table is narrow enough that under-selecting is a bigger risk than over-selecting. Operation code AND operation description both belong in response_columns together, not just one.
la_operation: Same pattern as erp_operation: small lookup table, prefer including all non-audit columns in pipeline_columns. Do not drop the operation type/category column even if not explicitly asked — it is frequently needed to disambiguate which operation the user means.
uom: UOM is a pure lookup table. pipeline_columns should include the UOM code and UOM description; response_columns should show the description, not the raw code, unless the user explicitly asked for the code.
mbom_operations: This module has the widest tables in the schema — be deliberate about pipeline_columns here rather than including everything. Always include whatever IME/traceability identifier the question implies (serial, packet, work order) in pipeline_columns even if only referenced indirectly (e.g. 'that unit', 'this batch'). Operation-level configuration columns are pipeline_columns only when the question is about configuration/setup, not for simple lookup questions.
default: If the question only asks for identification or existence of a record, keep response_columns minimal (name/code + status). If the question asks for a comparison, listing, or report, response_columns should include every column the user would need to read the answer without asking a follow-up question. Never put pure join/foreign-key columns in response_columns unless the user's question is specifically about that relationship.
